method: fit 2023 -> predict 2024; real bills (HB/SB) only; score = % reduction in mean absolute error vs predicting the session base rate. Positive = better than guessing. Negative = WORSE than guessing.

thresholds.DISQUALIFIED: invalid measurement; see superseded_by for the corrected test and its result
thresholds.CONDITIONAL: helps one outcome, harms the other

text_versions.note: RETESTED PROPERLY 2026-08-01 — counting only versions dated ON OR BEFORE introduction (knowable at filing). +0.5%/+1.3% = NOISE. The original +77.9% was 100% leakage. No gem; settled.

patron_floor_win_rate.note: RETESTED PROPERLY 2026-08-01 — prior-session votes. -5.6%/-2.8% = HARMFUL. Settled.

patron_party_loyalty.note: RETESTED PROPERLY 2026-08-01 — prior-session votes. -2.0%/-1.9% = HARMFUL. Settled.

patron_agrees_with_cmte.note: RETESTED PROPERLY 2026-08-01 — PRIOR-session votes against the CURRENT committee roster (both knowable when the bill is referred). -17.1%/+1.6% = HARMFUL. Settled.

patron_prior_in_this_cmte.note: Helps on one outcome and is WORSE THAN GUESSING on the other — only ever usable for the outcome it was validated on, never as a general stat.

patron_agrees_with_current_cmte.note: Corrected form of `patron_agrees_with_cmte`. PRIOR-session votes against the CURRENT committee roster (both knowable when the bill is referred). -17.1%/+1.6% = HARMFUL. Settled.

dls_tag.note: ADHD round. ADHD/lobbyist frame's strongest tell — the DLS drafting clause after the final semicolon ('; penalty', '; report'). 13 buckets, real variation, no signal.

same_day_batch.note: ADHD round. How many bills the patron filed the same day.

names_locality.note: ADHD round. Catchline names a County/City/Town (a 'courtesy bill'). Only 34 of 2,284, so thin either way.

patron_absence.note: ADHD round. Share of X/A (not voting / abstain) responses. Proposed INDEPENDENTLY by three frames; dead.

filing_recency_band.note: ADHD round. When in the filing window the bill was introduced, as a percentile of HB/SB only. Raw rates 81/82/73/77% — real variation, non-monotonic, no usable signal.

catchline_segments.note: ADHD round. Semicolon count in the catchline. NO VARIATION: 2,274 of 2,284 have exactly 2 segments, so the 'omnibus catchline' tell does not exist in VA data.

how_to_read: Scores are per OUTCOME and do not transfer between them. 'survived' = got out of committee. 'passed' = passed its chamber of origin. Before proposing any stat, grep this file: if it is here, it has been tested and the result stands unless the METHOD changes (new sessions, a fixed definition, or a corrected leak).

blocked_not_tested.section_citations: Needs the count of Code of Virginia sections a bill touches. The CATCHLINE contains no § symbols (0 of 2,284) and full bill text is not published in bulk. NOT TESTED — do not record as dead.
blocked_not_tested.draft_lead_time: Needs the gap between drafting and filing. Full_text_date1 IS the introduction date by construction in every row, so this dataset contains no drafting timeline at all. NOT TESTED.
blocked_not_tested.prior_session_recurrence: Needs a prior session for the TRAINING year too. With only 2023+2024 usable (2022 is partial), the training year has no prior and the feature is constant in training. Needs a THIRD complete session. NOT TESTED.
blocked_not_tested.fiscal_note_footprint: Needs History_description parsing for impact-statement rows; deferred, and would need a structural source before shipping.
blocked_not_tested.cross_chamber_companion: Needs text similarity across chambers; the similarity tooling exists (W2/W3/W4) but catchline-only matching is weak. Deferred.

companion_divergent_majority_standing.design: Companion pairs = same session, both chambers, identical title. DIVERGENT = one side passed, the other did not. Content is held constant, so the surviving side's advantage is attributable to what differs (chamber, committee, patron).
companion_divergent_majority_standing.pool: 11 regular sessions 2017-2027, Open States bulk CSV
caveats: 136 sides had no resolvable party or chamber majority
some title groups hold 3+ bills, so side-counts exceed 2x the pair count
chamber majority derived from the distinct sponsoring roster, not an external roster
companion_divergent_majority_standing.why_it_matters: Every prior test of majority standing had bill CONTENT as a confound. Here the text is identical, so this is the cleanest confirmation available.

Q3_what_gets_a_minority_bill_through.pool: 8,154 minority-patron HB/SB, 11 regular sessions 2017-2027, Open States
Q3_what_gets_a_minority_bill_through.why_it_matters: The only finding so far that names an ACTION rather than describing a situation. Recruiting a majority co-patron, or getting a majority member to carry the companion, is something an advocacy org can actually do.
Q3_what_gets_a_minority_bill_through.caveat: CORRELATIONAL. Bills that attract majority co-patrons may be less partisan to begin with, so the co-patron could be a symptom of an easy bill rather than a cause of the win. TESTABLE against the 504 divergent companion pairs, where text is held constant.
Q3_what_gets_a_minority_bill_through.status: confound test PASSED — cleared for use, with n=42 stated alongside it

confound_test.design: Divergent companion pairs (one side passed, one died) where BOTH chief patrons are in the minority and the two sides DIFFER in whether they have a majority-party co-patron. Text identical, chief-patron standing identical — co-patron composition is the only thing left.
confound_test.verdict: SURVIVES. The 61%-vs-31% headline is not merely a symptom of easy bills attracting co-patrons — with the bill held literally identical, the version carrying a majority co-patron won 3 times in 4.
confound_test.caveat: n=42, small by construction: requiring divergence AND both-minority chiefs AND differing co-patron status is restrictive. The split is lopsided enough that chance is an unlikely explanation, but re-check as sessions accumulate rather than treating it as settled.

findings_2026_08_02._pool: 22,659 HB/SB across 18 Open States sessions (2023S1 excluded as a duplicate of 2023). Companion pairing = exact title OR same subject-half + >=0.6 title-token overlap; recall measured at 92-95% vs abstract-derived truth. 4,424 pairs, 925 divergent.

co_patron_dose_response.read: The FIRST majority co-patron does most of the work: +26 points. After that, diminishing returns.

co_patron_by_chamber.read: Bigger lever in the House (+32) than the Senate (+26) — consistent with the House being the real filter.

seniority.read: Mid-career outperforms veterans in BOTH roles. Unexplained; possibly veterans in the minority carry harder bills.

money_committee_MYTH.read: NO EFFECT with content held constant. Money committees are where expensive bills go, not where bills die.

negative_space_minority_bills.read: Eightfold spread. Every worst is House, every best is Senate.

reintroduction.read: One in three failed bills returns; one in three of those wins. But a returning bill passes BELOW the overall baseline — coming back is not the same as winning.

governor.read: The amendment power is used TWICE as often as the veto, and works more than half the time. The reconvened session matters more than the veto.

where_to_file.read: Same bill, both chambers, one committee passed and its counterpart killed. Directly actionable filing advice.

findings_2026_08_02.topic_source: Virginia titles are 'Topic; what it does.' The subject-half is LIS's own drafting convention, available on all 22,659 bills — 7,825 distinct topics. Not our invention, and it needs no separate subject file (Open States publishes none).

committee_rate_varies_BY_TOPIC.H Finance: overall 37% — real property tax 63%, state income tax 19% (38 of 198). 44-pt spread.
committee_rate_varies_BY_TOPIC.S Education and Health: overall 52% — school boards 62%, certificate of public need 20%. 42-pt spread.
committee_rate_varies_BY_TOPIC.read: A committee's headline rate is often misleading. Validation signal: certificate-of-public-need surfacing as the worst topic in its committee is a well-known VA fight the method found unprompted.

barely matters.income tax, state: 35/147 (24%) vs 10/125 (8%) — 16 pts, but BOTH sides are low

minority_penalty_VARIES_BY_TOPIC.read: THE STRONGEST WAR-ROOM FINDING SO FAR. The minority penalty is not a constant — it runs from 38 points (firearms: 2 of 85 in 18 sessions) to 8 points (ABC). Tells an advocate when patron party is the whole game and when it is nearly irrelevant.
minority_penalty_VARIES_BY_TOPIC.caveat: Topic pooled across committees and chambers; minimum 40 bills per side. Not yet split by control regime.

_answered.house_volume_confound: Rates were used throughout, not counts, so raw volume is normalised (House 4,677 minority bills vs Senate 3,477; 25% vs 39%).
_answered.co_patron_moderate_bill_confound: Ruled out by the identical-text test — 32 of 42 divergent pairs, same bill on both sides.

_CONTROL_CORRECTION.bug: Chamber control was DERIVED by counting distinct chief patrons by party. It got 2 of 11 sessions wrong — 2022 Senate (said Republican, was Democratic) and 2023 (said House Democratic, was Republican; Senate unresolved). A near-tied chamber cannot survive the few percent of members whose party will not resolve by name. Same failure mode as the earlier voting-bloc derivation that inverted the 2023 House 52-48.
_CONTROL_CORRECTION.fix: CONTROL is now a pinned table from the historical record in corpus.py, and a session with no pinned entry is SKIPPED rather than guessed.
_CONTROL_CORRECTION.impact: Small — 2 of 18 sessions. Every headline held: co-patron lever 61%/31% -> 60%/29%; firearms minority 2 of 85 -> 2 of 91 (2%); ABC penalty 8 -> 11 points. Ordering and magnitudes unchanged.
_CONTROL_CORRECTION.lesson: Any aggregate built from a name-matched party label is unreliable where the margin is thin. Validate the aggregate against a known truth, not the per-item match rate.

UNAVAILABLE.firearms: ZERO minority-patron firearms bills acquired a majority co-patron in 18 sessions

co_patron_lever_by_topic.read: IMPORTANT TEMPERING of the headline lever. It works on consensus-adjacent topics and is either useless or entirely unavailable on the genuinely partisan ones. Nobody crosses the aisle on guns, so the best advice we have does not exist where an advocate needs it most.

symmetry_across_control_INCONCLUSIVE.design: Same topic, House only, minority side, compared under Republican rule (2017-19, 2022-23) and Democratic rule (2020-21, 2024-27).
symmetry_across_control_INCONCLUSIVE.result: Only 6 House topics clear 15 minority bills under BOTH parties, and they are mixed: ABC 55% under R vs 30% under D; electric utilities 26% under R vs 9% under D. Firearms does not qualify at all.
symmetry_across_control_INCONCLUSIVE.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE and recorded as such. 18 sessions is not enough to separate 'the institution penalises the minority' from 'this particular minority'. Not fixable by more slicing.

_TOPIC_SOURCE_CORRECTION.found: 2026-08-02, owner challenge: 'where are you getting these topics, are these the topics that LIS assigns? otherwise isnt this kind of useless because it relies on you deriving the topic?'
_TOPIC_SOURCE_CORRECTION.answer: He was right. The earlier 'topics' were MINE — the title's subject-half, split at the semicolon. 7,825 distinct fragments, a long tail rather than a taxonomy.
_TOPIC_SOURCE_CORRECTION.LIS_has_a_real_one: CiBillSubjects.csv — 1,561 distinct subjects, ~2 per bill, full coverage. Cached for 231 and 241.
_TOPIC_SOURCE_CORRECTION.head_to_head: Same 2 sessions, same bills, same method, only the label differs. LIS subjects: 15 topics clear 25+ bills per side. Title-derived: ZERO. The derived version only ever 'worked' because pooling 18 sessions accumulated enough per fragment.
_TOPIC_SOURCE_CORRECTION.consequence: All earlier topic-level numbers (firearms 2/91, ABC 48%) are DERIVED-LABEL results and are demoted. Not deleted — they used a consistent label across 18 sessions — but they must not be presented as LIS subject categories.
_TOPIC_SOURCE_CORRECTION.coverage_limit: LIS subjects exist for 2023 and 2024 only. A learned title-phrase -> LIS-subject bridge covers just 42% of the other 18,166 bills, so it is not a basis for a user-facing number.
_TOPIC_SOURCE_CORRECTION.fix: Ask DLAS for CiBillSubjects.csv for older sessions — small, specific, and it unlocks topic analysis across the whole window.

minority_penalty_by_LIS_SUBJECT_2023_202.pool: 4,345 bills with both a LIS subject and resolved standing (2023 + 2024)
minority_penalty_by_LIS_SUBJECT_2023_202.read: THE AUTHORITATIVE VERSION of the topic finding. Two sessions, LIS's own taxonomy, and it produces a cleaner and larger set of usable categories than 18 sessions of derived labels.

incorporation_who_survives_a_merge.pool: 677 absorbed->survivor pairs, found from LIS's own explicit action text ('Incorporated by ... (HB158-McClure)'). 18 sessions.

co_patron_count.confound: 69% of the time the ABSORBED bill's patron becomes a co-patron of the survivor, mechanically inflating the count

standing.read: Of 210 cross-standing merges, the majority patron's version wins 82%.

incorporation_who_survives_a_merge.seniority: survivor more senior 178 of 315 (57%) — near noise
incorporation_who_survives_a_merge.THE_INSIGHT: Co-patron COUNT is NOISE for predicting whether a bill passes (+0.3%, tested and filed as noise) but 83% for predicting WHICH of two competing bills is chosen. It is a SELECTION signal, not a survival signal — it does not help a bill pass, but when two versions are on the table it decides whose name stays on the one that moves.
incorporation_who_survives_a_merge.war_room_use: If a competing bill exists on the same subject, co-patron count is the thing that decides which version survives the merge. That is actionable and it is invisible in any single-bill view.

_LEAKAGE_CAUGHT_NOT_REPORTED.re_referral: 59% vs 0% — passing REQUIRES a second-chamber referral, so re-referral is downstream of the outcome
_LEAKAGE_CAUGHT_NOT_REPORTED.amended_or_substituted: 81% vs 25% — bills get amended because they are moving
_LEAKAGE_CAUGHT_NOT_REPORTED.subcommittee: 56% vs 38% — softer, but a bill that dies on arrival never reaches subcommittee
_LEAKAGE_CAUGHT_NOT_REPORTED.note: All three caught BEFORE being reported as findings. Same class as text_versions. Recorded so nobody re-derives them and gets excited.

WAITING_TIME_the_first_live_signal.why_it_is_different: Every other finding is STATIC — patron party, committee, chamber and topic are fixed on day one, so they are useful once and then wallpaper. This one CHANGES during the session, which is what a war room is for.
WAITING_TIME_the_first_live_signal.definition: Days from a bill's own introduction to the committee's first recorded decision (reported / PBI / tabled / stricken / continued / incorporated). A bill never decided counts as unheard at every N — that is the modal death and it must not be excluded.
WAITING_TIME_the_first_live_signal.read: Roughly halves. A minority-patron bill unheard after five weeks passes 19% of the time. Flattens after day 35 — beyond that, more waiting does not make it worse, it is already bad.
WAITING_TIME_the_first_live_signal.war_room_use: The only stat found so far that a war room can raise UNPROMPTED: 'HB1234 has sat 24 days without a committee decision; bills in that position pass 34%.' Updates weekly, needs no user input.
two_errors_fixed_getting_here: Session-day was measured from the earliest PREFILING date (November), not from convening, so 'day 7' was mid-prefile and the curve was meaningless.
The pool was conditioned on span>=N, i.e. on the bill still being alive at N — which is the thing being measured. It produced a spurious U-shape rising to 77%.

minority_penalty_IS_INSTITUTIONAL.corrects: An earlier entry called this INCONCLUSIVE. That was wrong — I had only tested it BY TOPIC, where buckets were too thin, then generalised the failure to the whole question. The overall test needs no topics and has ample data.

House.verdict: +29 vs +30. The House treats the minority the same regardless of who runs it. Per-session gaps run +21 to +39 across all nine with no party pattern. THIS IS THE INSTITUTION, NOT THE PARTY.

Senate.verdict: NOT symmetric, and the base levels differ sharply (41% vs 68% for majority patrons). Report separately; do not average with the House.

subject_classifier_solution.problem: LIS subject codes exist for 2023-2024 only. The owner will not contact DLAS before commercial launch, so the gap cannot be closed by asking.
subject_classifier_solution.solution: Train on the 4,345 bills where BOTH the title and LIS's real subjects are known, then label the other ~18,000. Naive Bayes over title tokens.
subject_classifier_solution.how_to_use_it: INTERNAL CALIBRATION ONLY. Standard #3 bars a derived label from the lobbyist-facing path; a predicted subject must never be shown to a user as if LIS assigned it.
subject_classifier_solution.statistical_caveat: ~23% label error ATTENUATES effects toward zero. So a finding that survives noisy labels is real but UNDERSTATED, and a null is not proof of absence. Directionally safe, magnitudes conservative.
subject_classifier_solution.unlocks: Subject-level analysis across 18 sessions instead of 2 — the difference between 4,345 bills and 22,659.

subject_classifier_ATTEMPTS.goal: Owner asked for 95%+ accuracy at 100% coverage. NOT REACHED — best blended ~91%.

tried_in_order.head-phrase exact lookup: 96.1% accurate but reaches only 41% of unlabelled bills

subject_classifier_ATTEMPTS.binding_constraint: 4,345 labelled examples, 43 classes, ~60 characters of text per bill, no embeddings available. Six approaches converge at 85-87% for the modelled portion.

doors_checked_and_shut.more labels from the authorized API: AdvancedLegislationSearch returns 28 fields for 20261 and NONE is a subject. The per-bill LegislationSubject service would be ~3,600 calls — ban risk, already ruled out in the vault.
doors_checked_and_shut.semantic embeddings: no sklearn or transformer library in this environment

subject_classifier_ATTEMPTS.RECOMMENDED_INSTEAD: Ship LOOKUP ONLY: 51% of bills at 96% accuracy, and leave the remainder UNLABELLED rather than wrongly labelled. ~9,600 confident labels plus 4,345 real ones. A 15% error rate silently attenuates every subject finding toward zero; an honest gap does not.
subject_classifier_ATTEMPTS.reopen_if: DLAS supplies CiBillSubjects for more sessions (triples the training set), or an embedding model becomes available.

_scope_confirmation.resolutions_excluded: VERIFIED 2026-08-02 at the owner's request. corpus.py filters to `^[HS]B ` — the corpus holds 13,968 HB and 8,691 SB and ZERO HJ/SJ/HR/SR. Every finding in this file is substantive bills only; commending and memorial resolutions never entered any denominator.

subject_coverage_IS_BIASED_do_not_extend.question: Owner, 2026-08-02: 'can we be sure the data you did collect isnt concentrated in a certain area... the ones you dont want to touch are a concentration of something that would inform our data.'
subject_coverage_IS_BIASED_do_not_extend.answer: HE WAS RIGHT. The reachable half is not a random sample, and the recommendation to ship lookup-only is WITHDRAWN.

bias_1_temporal.read: Reachability tracks whether we hold real labels for that session. Subject analysis across 18 sessions would be dominated by two recent ones.

bias_2_outcome.read: Five-point gap. The bills we cannot label pass MORE, so any subject pass-rate would run low.

bias_3_content_DECISIVE.read: These are the CONTESTED areas — firearms, hate crimes, parole, utilities — which is exactly where the largest minority penalties were found. Extending coverage with this gap would systematically underweight contentious policy and make the legislature look more consensual than it is.

subject_coverage_IS_BIASED_do_not_extend.DECISION: Subject-level findings are CONFINED to 2023-2024, where real LIS labels exist and coverage is complete. Do NOT extend subject analysis to other sessions using predicted or looked-up labels. Findings that do not use subjects (standing, committee, chamber, co-patron, waiting time) are unaffected and remain on all 18 sessions.
subject_coverage_IS_BIASED_do_not_extend.reopen_if: DLAS supplies CiBillSubjects for more sessions — which would close the gap rather than paper over it.
